uk-four-day-pilot.name: UK four-day week pilot
uk-four-day-pilot.outcome: 61 companies, about 2,900 staff; 71% reported lower burnout; 56 companies kept the shorter week
uk-four-day-pilot.limits: Companies opted in; results are self-reported surveys, not a controlled trial; organizers advocate for the policy.
uk-four-day-pilot.locator: "71% had reduced levels of 'burnout' by the end of the pilot"

iceland-trials.name: Iceland shorter working week trials
iceland-trials.outcome: From 2015-2019, about 2,500 workers moved to 35-36 hours with no pay cut; wellbeing rose; productivity and service provision remained the same or improved across the majority of trial workplaces; 86% of workforce later gained shorter hours or the right to them
iceland-trials.limits: Report by advocates (Autonomy and Alda); mostly public-sector workplaces; the 86% figure came through later union contracts, not the trials themselves.
iceland-trials.locator: "Worker wellbeing dramatically increased across a range of indicators"

who-burnout.name: WHO definition of burn-out in ICD-11
who-burnout.outcome: Burn-out defined as an occupational phenomenon from chronic workplace stress, with three dimensions; not a medical condition
who-burnout.limits: A classification, not a treatment; applies only to work, not other areas of life.
who-burnout.locator: "chronic workplace stress that has not been successfully managed"

maslach-six-areas.name: Maslach and Leiter's six areas of worklife
maslach-six-areas.place: University of Minnesota Extension interview with Christina Maslach
maslach-six-areas.outcome: Burnout traced to mismatches in workload, control, reward, community, fairness and values; each is a place to change
maslach-six-areas.limits: A research framework, not a personal test; the interview page gives one organizational example, not outcome data.
maslach-six-areas.locator: Section on the six areas; "positive pivot points"

australia-disconnect.name: Australia's right to disconnect
australia-disconnect.outcome: Workers may refuse to monitor or answer after-hours contact unless refusal is unreasonable; Fair Work Commission settles disputes
australia-disconnect.limits: Does not ban after-hours contact; small businesses covered only from August 2025; the opposition pledged repeal in 2024.
australia-disconnect.locator: "The law doesn't strictly prohibit employers from calling or messaging their workers after hours."

lorna-breen-act.name: Dr. Lorna Breen Health Care Provider Protection Act
lorna-breen-act.outcome: Signed March 18, 2022; federal grants for programs addressing burnout and mental health among health workers; named for Dr. Lorna Breen, an emergency room physician in New York City who took her own life on April 26, 2020
lorna-breen-act.limits: Grant program for health care only; funding needs renewal by Congress, and current status was not checked in this run.
lorna-breen-act.locator: "seeks to address burnout among healthcare workers"

lifeline-988.name: 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline
lifeline-988.outcome: Free call, text or chat, around the clock, for anyone in emotional distress, not only suicidal crisis
lifeline-988.limits: U.S. only; a crisis line, not ongoing care.

fmla.name: Family and Medical Leave Act
fmla.outcome: Up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave for a serious health condition or to care for family
fmla.limits: Unpaid; only for employers with 50+ staff nearby and workers with 12 months and 1,250 hours; some states add more.

eap-opm.name: Federal employee assistance program
eap-opm.outcome: Free, confidential assessments, short-term counseling and referrals for employees
eap-opm.limits: This page describes the federal program; private employers' programs vary in sessions and quality.
eap-opm.locator: "free and confidential assessments, short-term counseling, referrals"

pew-pto.name: Pew survey on unused paid time off
pew-pto.outcome: 46% of workers with paid time off take less than offered; 49% of them worry about falling behind; 43% feel badly about coworkers taking on additional work
pew-pto.limits: Survey of non-self-employed workers in February 2023; self-reported reasons.
pew-pto.locator: Reasons list: worry about falling behind at work (49%)

surgeon-general-framework.name: Surgeon General's Framework for Workplace Mental Health and Well-Being
surgeon-general-framework.outcome: Released October 20, 2022 by Surgeon General Dr. Vivek Murthy; five essentials for employers, including making sure workers are well rested and have paid leave
surgeon-general-framework.limits: Guidance only; no enforcement or outcome data.
surgeon-general-framework.locator: Protection from Harm: "ensuring workers are well-rested"

nlrb-concerted.name: Protected concerted activity under the National Labor Relations Act
nlrb-concerted.outcome: Employees acting together about working conditions are protected from retaliation, with or without a union
nlrb-concerted.limits: Must concern working conditions; protection can be lost through misconduct; enforcement takes time.
nlrb-concerted.locator: "engaged in with or on the authority of other employees"

ca-ratios-2010.name: Aiken study of California nurse staffing ratios
ca-ratios-2010.outcome: 29% of California nurses reported burnout versus 34% and 36% in states without ratios; 22,000+ nurses surveyed in 2006
ca-ratios-2010.limits: Reported on a nurses' union page that campaigns for ratios; cross-sectional survey.

ca-ratios-2025.name: 2025 study of California nurse burnout and ratios
ca-ratios-2025.outcome: 40% of California nurses reported high burnout versus 45% elsewhere, about 19% lower odds, attributed to ratios
ca-ratios-2025.limits: Publisher's blog summary; sample size not stated on the page; research on ratios is mixed overall.
ca-ratios-2025.locator: "40% of California nurses report high burnout"

eldercare-locator.name: Eldercare Locator
eldercare-locator.outcome: Free phone and text line, 1-800-677-1116, that connects older adults and caregivers with local services
eldercare-locator.limits: The page does not specifically promise respite care; staff point you to local agencies.
eldercare-locator.locator: "a public service of the Administration for Community Living"

copenhagen-burnout-inventory.name: Copenhagen Burnout Inventory
copenhagen-burnout-inventory.place: Copenhagen, Denmark: National Institute of Occupational Health (Borritz and Kristensen)
copenhagen-burnout-inventory.outcome: 19 questions in three scales: personal burnout (6), work burnout (7) and client burnout (6), each scored 0 to 100; the PUMA study counted 50 or more as a high degree of burnout
copenhagen-burnout-inventory.limits: The PDF does not state licensing or terms of use; normed on Danish adults and human-service workers; a research questionnaire, not a diagnosis, with no official clinical cutoff.
copenhagen-burnout-inventory.locator: Part two: Work burnout. "(First edition. February 2004)"

arch-respite-locator.name: ARCH National Respite Locator
arch-respite-locator.outcome: Directory that helps family caregivers find respite services in their state and local area; site supported by the federal Administration for Community Living; links a How to Pay for Respite guide
arch-respite-locator.limits: The page says the database "is not a complete list"; ARCH does not vet listed providers; it does not provide respite itself.
arch-respite-locator.locator: "not a complete list of all the respite programs that exist"

microsoft-japan.name: Microsoft Japan Work-Life Choice Challenge
microsoft-japan.outcome: Staff took five Fridays off in August 2019 with full pay, meetings were shortened; the company said the result was a productivity boost of 40%
microsoft-japan.limits: One month, one company, company-reported figure; the article does not say how productivity was measured.
microsoft-japan.locator: "The result, the company says, was a productivity boost of 40%."
